classification.difficultyReason: Derive a quadratic area model from a fixed perimeter and solve a strict quadratic inequality in context.

content.prompt: A rectangle has perimeter $22\text{ cm}$. Let one side have a length of $x\text{ cm}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write down an expression for the area $A$ of this rectangle in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
Let the other side have length $y\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}2x+2y&=22\\x+y&=11\\y&=11-x\\A&=x(11-x)\\A&=11x-x^2\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What values may $x$ take if $A>28\text{ cm}^2$?

answer.short:
$4<x<7$.

The quadratic is negative between its zeroes.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x(11-x)&>28\\11x-x^2-28&>0\\x^2-11x+28&<0\\(x-4)(x-7)&<0\end{align*}$$
The zeroes are $4$ and $7$. At $x=1$, $5$ and $8$, the product $(x-4)(x-7)$ is $18$, $-2$ and $4$, respectively. It is negative between the zeroes.
Hence $4<x<7$.
